newsitem.title: USA: CD Radio, Amer.Mobile win satellite radio licenses.
newsitem.headline: CD Radio, Amer.Mobile win satellite radio licenses.

text.p: CD Radio Inc and a unit of American Mobile Satellite Corp each won a license in a government auction Wednesday to provide a nationwide radio service that will be delivered via satellite and offer CD-quality reception.
CD Radio, based in Washington, DC, agreed to pay $83.3 million for one of the licenses that the Federal Communications Commission auctioned.
American Mobile Radio Corp, a unit of Reston, Va.-based, American Mobile Satellite, agreed to pay $89.9 million for the second license up for grabs.
The companies were among four participating in the FCC sale of digital audio radio licenses.
CD Radio expects to have its service in operation by the second half of 1999, delivering 50 stations of news, entertainment and other programs.
American Mobile Radio expects to be up and running in at least three years, delivering 25-35 channels of programming.
The FCC auction, which began Tuesday, lasted 25 rounds of bidding.
